data.theorem_title: For $s>1$, the Zipf harmonic sums tend to $\zeta(s)$
data.formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipf_genHarmonic_tendsto_zeta (s : ℝ) (hs : 1 < s) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => ((genHarmonic N s : ℝ) : ℂ)) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (riemannZeta s)) := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
data.natural_language_statement: If $s>1$, the generalized harmonic partial sums $H_{N,s}=\sum_{k=1}^{N}k^{-s}$ converge to Riemann's zeta function $\zeta(s)$. The formal limit takes place in $\mathbb C$ after casting the real sums, because Mathlib's `riemannZeta` is complex-valued.
data.source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law, section "Formal definition"; auxiliary lemma for the original ZipfLaw mission, derived from its displayed PMF and generalized harmonic sum.
